content.title: Oscars 2026 Tie In Live Action Short Film: Biggest Snubs & Surprises
content.text: Skip to main content Oscars Snubs And Surprises: From The Live-Action Short Tie To Films That Left Empty-Handed L-R: Michael B. Jordan in 'Sinners', Renate Reinsve in 'Sentimental Value' and Benicio del Toro in 'One Battle After Another' Warner Bros, Neon, Warner Bros Dame Anna Wintour snub of Anne Hathaway’s beautiful Oscars gown aside, several films were ignored or prevailed past others unexpectedly at Sunday’s 98th Oscars. Titles shut out completely included multiple nominees Marty Supreme, Bugonia, Train Dreams, The Secret Agent and more. RELATED: Oscars: ‘One Battle After Another’ Takes Best Picture, Director & Four Others; Jordan & Buckley Win Lead Acting Prizes: Full List Here’s what stood out most Sunday: Surprise – First Casting Oscar Goes To ‘One Battle After Another’Photo : Kevin Winter/Getty Images In one of the first surprises of the night, One Battle After Another‘s Cassandra Kulukundis won the inaugural Oscar for casting. Introduced by star Chase Infiniti, the casting director joked that she had won an Oscar before director Paul Thomas Anderson — he subsequently won three. Sinners casting director Francine Maisler, who won Casting Society‘s Artios Award for her work on the film, had been heavily favored to win in the category. Snub – ‘Marty Supreme’ Josh Safdie’s ping pong film starring Timothée Chalamet did not win a single trophy, despite nominations for Best Actor in a Lead Role, Best Directing, Best Picture and more. Chalamet, an early frontrunner in the Lead Actor category with wins at the Golden Globes and Critics’ Choice Awards, lost out to Sinners’ Michael B. Jordan. Surprise – ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ Wins Documentary FeaturePhoto : Kevin Winter/Getty Images Mr. Nobody Against Putin was a surprise winner in the Documentary Feature category. The Perfect Neighbor, Come See Me in the Good Light and even The Alabama Solution were considered more likely to win the trophy. Directed by David Borenstein and co-directed by Pavel “Pasha” Talankin (the titular ‘Mr. Nobody’), Mr. Nobody Against Putin went much of awards season without U.S. distribution before being acquired by Kino Lorber in early January. Snub – Ryan Coogler, DirectingPhoto : Kevin Winter/Getty Images Although he won for Best Original Screenplay, Sinners‘ Ryan Coogler lost the directing race to Paul Thomas Anderson and One Battle After Another, and then again for Best Picture. Sinners had enjoyed a surge late in the awards campaign, including an Best Ensemble win at the Actor Awards, making it a strong Best Picture contender. Surprise – Live-Action Short Film Tie Between ‘The Singers’ And ‘Two People Exchanging Saliva’ Presenter Kumail Nanjiani very coolly handled the pressure of presenting a tie between The Singers and Two People Exchanging Saliva, telling the audience to remain calm and “focus up” for the announcement of the results. This is the seventh time in Oscars history a tie has taken place, with the most recent one being in the Sound Editing category for Skyfall and Zero Dark Thirty in 2013. Snub – Stellan SkarsgårdPhoto : Kasper Tuxen/Neon/Everett Collection Sean Penn was favored to win the Best Supporting Actor Oscar, though Stellan Skarsgård had been nearly neck and neck with the One Battle After Another star, who didn’t make it to tonight’s ceremony. Skarsgård won over Penn at the Golden Globes, the one major award show this season that Penn did attend. Snub – ‘Bugonia’Photo : Focus Features / Courtesy Everett Collection Normally popular with the Academy, Yorgos’ Lanthimos and Emma Stone struck out with Bugonia despite Best Picture, Best Actress in a a Leading Role, Original Score and Adapted Screenplay nominations. Snub – ‘Train Dreams’Photo : Netflix / Courtesy Everett Collection Netflix’s Train Dreams didn’t win any awards either. The film had been up for Best Picture, Adapted Screenplay, Original Song and Cinematography. Snub – ‘The Secret Agent’ Cannes Film Festival double winner The Secret Agent and its star Wagner Moura walked away empty-handed as well tonight despite Best Picture, International Feature, Best Actor and Casting nominations and two Golden Globe wins.
